### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hereditary spastic paraplegia 31  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:25786)

**Proposed mechanism:** REEP1 (HGNC:25786) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic Reticulum protein processing and folding (GO:0006492); Endoplasmic Reticulum protein processing and folding (GO:0006492) —LEADS_TO→ Spasticity (HP:0002360); Endoplasmic Reticulum protein processing and folding (GO:0006492) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron disease (HP:0007148). Loss-of-function mutations in REEP1 disrupt normal endoplasmic reticulum protein processing and folding, leading to both spasticity and motor neuron disease.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in REEP1 that confers a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: rs141146020)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the precise role of REEP1 in ER protein homeostasis may reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative disorders characterized by spasticity and motor neuron degeneration.

#### 2. spinal muscular atrophy, distal, autosomal recessive, 6  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.724)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:25786)

**Proposed mechanism:** REEP1 (HGNC:25786) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic reticulum membrane organization (GO:0005783); Endoplasmic reticulum membrane organization (GO:0005783) —LEADS_TO→ Distal lower limb muscle weakness (HP:0002475); Endoplasmic reticulum membrane organization (GO:0005783) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function variants in REEP1 disrupt endoplasmic reticulum membrane organization, leading to distal lower limb muscle weakness in MONDO:0013884 and general muscle weakness in spinal muscular atrophy, distal, autosomal recessive, 6.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping sets of causal variants in REEP1 for each disease, or evidence that REEP1 variants causing one disease do not impact the other disease's primary phenotype. _(variant: rs12345678 (hypothetical variant with high frequency in gnomAD))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of REEP1 in ER membrane organization and its link to both distinct and overlapping neuromuscular phenotypes could inform therapeutic strategies targeting protein trafficking and ER homeostasis for both conditions.
